requirements.req_text: Safety. Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the most likely hazards you may encounter while working with robots and what you should do to anticipate, mitigate, prevent, and respond to these hazards. Describe the appropriate safety gear and clothing that should be used when working with robotics. (b) Discuss first aid and prevention for the types of injuries that could occur while participating in robotics activities and competitions, including cuts, eye injuries, and burns (chemical or heat).

pamphlet_excerpts: Moreinformation Aboutfirst: For moreinformation aboutfirst aid, see the First Aid meritbadge pamphlet.
Discuss Potential Hazards: Discuss with your counselor all the potential hazards stemmingfrom your project.
Proper Aid Cuts: Know the proper first aid for cuts, burns, andeye injuries.
Dress Appropriately Working: To avoid minor cuts and scrapes, be sure you dress appropriately when working on your robot, for instance, jeans, boots, gloves, and so on.
step_by_step_procedure: Treat Minor Cuts: Treat minor cuts and scrapes by flushingthe area with clean water for at least five minutes, or untilall foreign matter appears to be washed away.
Apply Tripleantibiotic: Apply tripleantibiotic ointment (if appropriate and if there are no knownallergies) and cover with a dry, sterile bandage.
Working Close Supervision: Working under close supervision of a responsible adultand being careful when you work with materials that can causeburns will help prevent.
Chemical Burns Simportant: For chemical burns, it’simportant to quickly brush off as much of the chemical as possible using a gloved hand.

pamphlet_excerpts: Autonomous Robot Controlled: An autonomous robot is controlled by its internal computer.
Autonomous Robot System: An autonomous robot system is much like the humanautonomic system (a part of the nervous system thatcontrols involuntary actions like heartbeat.
Operates Regulates Itself: It operates and regulates itself without our awareness or interference.
Common Computer Robot: A common computer and robot interface is a keyboard.
step_by_step_procedure: Autonomous Robots: Autonomous robots are generallyprogrammed by the operator using a keyboard.
Program Directs Robot: The program directs the robot through thecontroller, a small computer on the robot.
Common Programming: Another common programming interfacefor autonomous robots is a teach pendant.
Teach Pendants Similar: Teach pendants are similar to a handheldvideo-game controller that has a small videoscreen.

requirements.lead_text: Design, Build, Program, Test. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Design, Build, Program, Test. Do the following: (a) With your counselor's approval, choose a task for the robot or robotic subsystem that you plan to build. Include sensor feedback and programming in the task. Document this information in your robot engineering notebook. (b) Design your robot. The robot design should use sensors and programming and have at least 2 degrees of freedom. Document the design in your robot engineering notebook using drawings and a written description. (c) Build a robot or robotic subsystem of your original design to accomplish the task you chose for requirement 4(a). (d) Discuss with your counselor the programming options available for your robot. Then do ONE of the following: (1) Program your robot to perform the task you chose for your robot in 4(a). Include a sample of your program's source code in your robot engineering notebook. (2) Prepare a flowchart of the desired steps to program your robot for accomplishing the task in 4(a). Include procedures that show activities based on sensor inputs. Place this in your robot engineering notebook. (e) Test your robot and record the results in your robot engineering notebook. Include suggestions on how you could improve your robot, as well as pictures or sketches of your finished robot.

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Identify three career opportunities that would use skills and knowledge in robotics. Pick one and research the training, education, certification requirements, experience, and expenses associated with entering the field. Research the prospects for employment, starting salary, advancement opportunities and career goals associated with this career. Discuss what you learned with your counselor and whether you might be interested in this career. (b) Identify how you might use the skills and knowledge in robotics to pursue a personal hobby. Research the additional training required, expenses, and affiliation with organizations that would help you maximize the enjoyment and benefit you might gain from it. Discuss what you learned with your counselor and share what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursued this.

Few Possible Career: Only a few of the possible career paths arediscussed here.
Classesas Possible Math: Take as many classesas possible in math, physics, computers, and design.
Muchpractical Hands-on: Get as muchpractical, hands-on experience as possible by participating in clubsor organizations pertaining to robotics or engineering.
step_by_step_procedure: Than High School: You will need more than a high school degree to work withrobots.
Want Robotics Technician: If you want to be a robotics technician, many junior orcommunity colleges offer robotics and automation associatedegrees.
Robotics Technicians Operate: Robotics technicians operate and maintain the robots; ifyou want to design robots you will need to get anengineering degree.
People Seek Career: Most people who seek a career in robotics major inmechanical, electrical, structural, biomedical, or industrialengineering or computer science.
